A former Salomon Brothers bond trader, he built a substantial fortune through leveraged buyouts at Wesray, then established William E. Simon & Sons with his two sons to pursue merchant banking investments.

long_biography.plain_text:
William Simon helped turn the profits of the Los Angeles Olympics into lasting support for American athletes. As president of the U.S. Olympic Committee during the 1984 Games, he worked on the organisation's role in staging the event. He then became the first chairman of the U.S. Olympic Foundation, which invested the Games' surplus to support future training and competition.

His charitable work also involved direct personal service. Simon and his family visited homeless teenagers at Covenant House, joining activities and helping in the kitchen. He required directors of his own foundation to undertake 150 hours of hands-on service each year, making practical participation part of their responsibilities.
